core_obligations: Read the two hypotheses as saying that the two Koszul complexes are finite free resolutions of the corresponding quotients (proof lines 7688-7694).
Identify the quotient by all the elements with the total complex of the tensor product of the two Koszul complexes (proof lines 7694-7700).
Use the first hypothesis to replace the first factor by the quotient by the first block (proof lines 7700-7704).
Recognise the result as the Koszul complex of the images of the second block over that quotient, which gives the statement (proof lines 7704-7708).
proof_roadmap: Translate the hypotheses into resolutions (proof lines 7688-7694).
Tensor the complexes and identify the total complex (proof lines 7694-7700).
Replace one factor by the quotient (proof lines 7700-7704).
Recognise the Koszul complex over the quotient and conclude (proof lines 7704-7709).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the truncation companion of the juxtaposition statement for Koszul-regular sequences, and its proof is a 22-line chain of quasi-isomorphisms. Reading the hypotheses as saying that the two Koszul complexes resolve the corresponding quotients, it identifies the quotient by all the elements with the Koszul complex of the full sequence, rewrites that complex as the total complex of the tensor product of the two Koszul complexes, replaces the first factor by the quotient by the first block using the first hypothesis, and recognises the result as the Koszul complex of the images of the second block over that quotient, which is exactly Koszul-regularity of those images. Every step is attributed to a named statement and the chain is displayed.
